transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-18
Time: 10:00am PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Chen (Redwood AE), Alex Murphy (Redwood SE), Rosa Alvarez (Redwood CSM); Sarah Patel (VertexHealth Head of ML), Mark Ruiz (Platform Lead), Priya Singh (Security & Compliance), Devon Lee (SRE)

Summary (auto): Weekly POC check-in. Focus on rollout sequencing: canary, A/B, monitoring, runbooks, cutover date options, security artifacts outstanding.

[00:00:10] Jamie Chen: hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. quick agenda — review where we are on the pilot metrics, agree canary strategy, monitoring and runbook owners, and decide on a tentative cutover window.
[00:00:25] Sarah Patel: yep thanks Jamie, appreciate it. we went through the latest test results yesterday, overall latency looks good but the tail is still a little jittery for long prompts.
[00:00:35] Alex Murphy: yeah the p50/p90 are solid, p99 spikes when sequence length goes above 2k tokens, that's expected with the current batching profile and kv-cache behaviour. we have a tuning plan though.
[00:00:50] Mark Ruiz: hi team, from infra side we need to lock the change freeze windows. we have a major data pipeline deploy on 2026-03-29 so cutover can't be that week.
[00:01:05] Jamie Chen: noted, mark. so tentatively customer suggested week was early April, does that still work?
[00:01:12] Devon Lee: early april works but we need to run a dry-run with our SREs to simulate load and failovers.

[00:02:00] Alex Murphy: quick recap of what we tested: throughput baseline against the dedicated host (quantized model) at 40k tokens/min with 95% success under the current batching config. error rate was ~0.3% with transient timeouts during burst tests.
[00:02:18] Sarah Patel: that error rate is acceptable for a pilot but for production we need it <0.1%. what are the knob options?
[00:02:30] Alex Murphy: main levers are: reduce max batch size to lower queuing latency, enable prefix caching for repeated prompts, and a slightly higher provisioned concurrency for the canary. also smaller sequence-length-aware kernel selection which we can tune on the runtime.
[00:02:47] Jamie Chen: one tradeoff to call out — increasing provisioned concurrency reduces tail latency but raises cost. we should define SLOs for the canary to justify that delta.

[00:04:10] Priya Singh: on security — thanks for the SOC2 packet you shared. I skimmed it; a few items to confirm: encryption-at-rest key ownership, KMS integration details for private deployment, and audit-log retention policy. can you confirm where those live?
[00:04:28] Jamie Chen: yes — we shared a link to the security pack in the drive (link noted), and Alex can attach the KMS integration doc. short answer: for Private we support customer-managed KMS, audit logs are configurable up to 7 years for enterprise.
[00:04:42] Alex Murphy: i will upload the KMS HSM workflow and the audit-log retention table after this call.

[00:05:15] Rosa Alvarez: quick ops question — do we have a runbook template for cutover and rollback?
[00:05:23] Alex Murphy: we do — i can share a runbook template that covers pre-cutover checks, canary gating, monitor thresholds, and a rollback checklist. it also includes sample Prometheus/Grafana dashboards and alerting rules.
[00:05:40] Sarah Patel: great. can we also include a short playbook for model fallback behavior? e.g., if latency > 3s for 5 minutes, fallback to smaller model variant or to cached response.
[00:05:52] Alex Murphy: yes, fallback policies are supported. we usually suggest a tiered fallback: first smaller quantized variant, then a cached deterministic response, then a circuit-breaker to stop calls.

[00:07:00] Jamie Chen: canary strategy choices — two main options: progressive canary by percent of traffic (A/B style) or shadow canary where traffic is mirrored and only monitored. which does vertex prefer?
[00:07:12] Sarah Patel: we prefer progressive canary so we get real user signals, but we want strict gate metrics.
[00:07:18] Mark Ruiz: progressive makes sense, but we need the ability to instantly roll back. our platform team needs automation hooks for the rollback.
[00:07:28] Alex Murphy: we can wire the rollout to an automated policy in Redwood: if SLOs breach (error rate, p95 latency, or quality regression metrics) the router moves 100% back to baseline model. we can also provide a manual toggle in console for immediate cut.

[00:09:00] Devon Lee: what metrics should be in the gate? latency p95 and p99? error rate? quality drop?
[00:09:10] Jamie Chen: recommended minimum gate: error rate <0.2%, p95 <X ms (we'll put exact number after your baseline), p99 not exceeding Y ms for more than 5 minutes, and a small automated quality check using a holdout prompt set (we run synthetic evals every minute).
[00:09:30] Sarah Patel: can we include business-level KPI as well — e.g., deflection rate for support flows or NPS delta for user sample?
[00:09:38] Rosa Alvarez: yes include the business KPI as a secondary gate — but primary must be system SLOs.

[00:11:20] Alex Murphy: about A/B — if you want to test parameter changes (prompt templates, temperature), we recommend traffic-split A/B with experiment tracking. Redwood supports that via per-route rollout configs.
[00:11:33] Mark Ruiz: we will likely A/B prompt templates in prod after cutover, not during initial canary. initial canary should be model+infra only.

[00:13:00] Jamie Chen: runbook owners — propose:
- Vertex: Mark and Devon for infra steps and final go/no-go
- Vertex: Priya for security sign-off
- Redwood: Alex for providing runbook template and monitoring dashboards, Rosa to coordinate dry-run scheduling
Does that mapping work?
[00:13:15] Mark Ruiz: yes that's fine.
[00:13:20] Priya Singh: yes, as long as I get the security artifacts.

[00:14:40] Alex Murphy: quick note about monitoring: we'll provide a Grafana dashboard with token-level cost, per-route latency breakdown, error heatmap, and canary traffic percentage. alert rules will push to your PagerDuty escalation policy.
[00:14:56] Sarah Patel: can we get a sample of the dashboard? a screenshot or a live link?
[00:15:02] Alex Murphy: i'll share a live sample link and the JSON dashboard export.

[00:16:30] Jamie Chen: timeline check — proposed steps:
- this week: finalize runbook and security checklist
- next week: dry-run with SRE + simulation of failover
- following week: staged canary (0-10-25-50) over 48 hours
- target cutover week: 2026-04-05 (tentative)
Any blockers?
[00:16:50] Sarah Patel: the main blocker is compliance sign-off on KMS and log retention; Priya will confirm.
[00:16:58] Priya Singh: i'll confirm by 2026-03-24; if there are gaps we'll list compensating controls.

[00:18:20] Mark Ruiz: two infra items — change freeze windows (can't cutover 2026-03-29) and capacity reservation for dedicated pool during canary. cost impact?
[00:18:32] Jamie Chen: cost delta depends on provisioned concurrency; we can provide a short spreadsheet with cost at different concurrency/traffic levels. i'll include that when i send the runbook.

[00:20:10] Devon Lee: what about rollback automation hooks — we need a webhook or API to the platform to toggle routes. how is that secured?
[00:20:20] Alex Murphy: we expose a control-plane API secured via mTLS and RBAC. we can create a service account for your SRE team with scoped permissions to toggle routes. KMS keys are used to sign tokens. i'll document the exact endpoints.

[00:22:00] Sarah Patel: on data residency — reminder: some PHI flows must stay in us-east-1. does Redwood let us pin region per-route?
[00:22:09] Jamie Chen: yes — routing policies support region pinning and automatic fallback to approved regions only. we'll capture that in the rollout config.

[00:24:00] Rosa Alvarez: can we schedule the dry-run now? who needs to be there?
[00:24:06] Mark Ruiz: Platform, SRE, and ML infra. Priya for quick security verification. Sarah, Devon, and Alex from your side.
[00:24:16] Rosa Alvarez: i'll send a Doodle and propose slots for 2026-03-25 and 2026-03-26.

[00:26:10] Jamie Chen: open questions from Redwood side — we wanted to confirm whether you want a shadow run in prod for the first 24 hours or a small progressive percent.
[00:26:20] Sarah Patel: progressive percent. start with 1% for a few hours then move to 10, etc.
[00:26:30] Alex Murphy: ok we'll prepare an automated rollout schedule (1%, 5%, 10%, 25%, 50%, 100%) with gate checks at each step.

[00:28:00] Priya Singh: re legal/procurement — any outstanding T&Cs delaying cutover?
[00:28:08] Jamie Chen: procurement is in parallel. Rosa, any updates?
[00:28:15] Rosa Alvarez: legal has one small change on data processing appendix; i'm following up with contracts. shouldn't block pilot cutover but will need final sign-off for production SLA.

[00:30:00] Alex Murphy: small technical note — during the canary we recommend enabling KV cache warmup to reduce cold-start tail. it's a config change in the runtime. it'll increase memory usage slightly.
[00:30:14] Mark Ruiz: call that out in the runbook, we need to budget memory.

[00:32:00] Jamie Chen: recap of risks and mitigations:
- Risk: tail latency spikes -> Mitigation: provisioned concurrency + KV cache warmup + smaller batch size for canary
- Risk: quality regression -> Mitigation: synthetic evals + holdout prompt set gating
- Risk: compliance gaps -> Mitigation: Priya to list gaps + compensating controls

[00:34:10] Sarah Patel: thanks, that covers it. final ask — can we get a short checklist (2 pages) for execs summarizing cutover plan and KPIs?
[00:34:20] Jamie Chen: yes we will send an exec one-pager when we share the runbook.

[00:36:00] Rosa Alvarez: action review — i'll summarize and send calendar invites for dry-run. Jamie will send runbook and cost spreadsheet. Alex will share dashboards and benchmark CSV. Priya will confirm compliance items. Mark will confirm cutover windows.

[00:38:00] Priya Singh: one more thing — retention of logs for 7 years, need proof of chain-of-custody for audit, can Redwood provide sample audit log extracts?
[00:38:12] Alex Murphy: yes we can provide sample extracts and a description of chain-of-custody for logs.

[00:40:00] Jamie Chen: ok final quick timeline and responsibilities — send next_steps in follow-up email. thanks everyone, meeting adjourned.

Attachments referenced: security_packet_v1.pdf (link in drive), runbook_template_v2.md (to be shared), canary_dashboard_sample (Grafana link), throughput_benchmark_2026-03-17.csv (Alex to attach).

Transcript end.
